sentiment.rationale: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to 'low- to mid-teens' growth from a prior unspecified level, and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was raised to 'at least 35%'. The raise is attributed to organic momentum in growth initiatives, monetization improvements, and durable ADR, not primarily to FX or one-time items. Management language is confident and forward-looking, with no material risks or hedges raised in Q&A.

summary.revenue: Q1 2026 revenue of $2.7 billion, up 18% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance.
summary.eps: Net income was $160 million; adjusted EBITDA was $519 million, up 24% year-over-year. EPS not explicitly stated.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2026 revenue growth raised to low- to mid-teens; adjusted EBITDA margin raised to at least 35%. Q2 2026 revenue expected $3.54B–$3.6B (14–16% YoY growth).
summary.margin: Adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be at least 35% for full year 2026. Q1 free cash flow margin 36% on trailing 12 months.
key_risks: Conflict in the Middle East causing an approximate 100-basis-point headwind to nights and seats booked growth in Q1 and expected to continue in Q2.
Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty, including tariff uncertainty affecting travel patterns.
Tougher comps in the back half of 2026 against the rollout of Reserve Now, Pay Later.
key_opportunities: Reserve Now, Pay Later driving longer lead times, higher ADR, and a meaningful lift to all booking metrics.
World Cup expected to be the largest event in Airbnb's history, with over 100,000 new listings added.
AI initiatives: 60% of code written by AI, AI Assistant resolving over 40% of customer issues without human agent, cost per booking down 10% YoY.
Hotel pilot scaling rapidly, with top-line metrics growing more than double the overall business.
Expansion markets (Brazil, Japan, India) growing at roughly twice the rate of core markets.
First-time booker growth accelerating to 10%, highest since 2022.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Brian Chesky stated 'Airbnb had a strong start to 2026' and 'we're really excited about the year ahead and our guidance reflects that,' while Ellie Mertz said 'we remain optimistic about our continued momentum.'

evidence.claim: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to low- to mid-teens growth.
evidence.quote: We're raising our guidance for 2026 and now expect year-over-year revenue growth to accelerate to low- to mid-teens.

evidence.claim: Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to at least 35%.
evidence.quote: We anticipate our adjusted EBITDA margin to be at least 35%.

evidence.claim: Q1 2026 revenue was $2.7 billion, up 18% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance.
evidence.quote: Revenue grew 18% year-over-year to $2.7 billion, which exceeded the high end of our guidance.

evidence.claim: Q1 2026 net income was $160 million; adjusted EBITDA was $519 million, up 24% year-over-year.
evidence.quote: Our net income was $160 million, while adjusted EBITDA was $519 million, up 24% year-over-year, also exceeding guidance.

evidence.claim: Q2 2026 revenue guidance is $3.54B–$3.6B, representing 14–16% year-over-year growth.
evidence.quote: In Q2, we expect to generate revenue of $3.54 billion to $3.6 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 14% to 16%.

evidence.claim: Conflict in the Middle East caused an approximate 100-basis-point headwind to nights and seats booked growth in Q1.
evidence.quote: Nights and seats booked grew 9% after accounting for an approximate 100-basis-point headwind from the conflict in the Middle East.

evidence.claim: Reserve Now, Pay Later is driving longer lead times, higher ADR, and a meaningful lift to all booking metrics.
evidence.quote: Reserve Now, Pay Later is driving a meaningful lift to all booking metrics, net of cancellations. We believe this is a longer term competitive benefit, locking in earlier calendar share and better aligning our payment options with guest preferences.

evidence.claim: World Cup expected to be the largest event in Airbnb's history, with over 100,000 new listings added.
evidence.quote: The World Cup is the next chapter in our events strategy, and we expect to host more guests than any event in Airbnb's history. Since we started outreach in October, over 100,000 homes have listed on Airbnb for the first time.

evidence.claim: AI initiatives: 60% of code written by AI, AI Assistant resolving over 40% of issues without human agent, cost per booking down 10% YoY.
evidence.quote: Nearly 60% of the code our engineers produce is now written by AI... over 40% of issues are now resolved without a human agent... We've seen the cost per booking decrease about 10% year-over-year in Q1.

evidence.claim: Hotel pilot scaling rapidly, with top-line metrics growing more than double the overall business.
evidence.quote: In the last couple quarters, what we've seen is that all the top line metrics for hotels are growing more than double that of the entire business.

evidence.claim: Expansion markets growing at roughly twice the rate of core markets.
evidence.quote: Net nights for expansion markets grew at roughly twice the rate of our core markets.

evidence.claim: First-time booker growth accelerating to 10%, highest since 2022.
evidence.quote: Growth in first-time bookers also accelerated to 10%. Now, this is the highest growth rate since 2022.
Brian Chesky: 'Airbnb had a strong start to 2026.' 'We're really excited about the year ahead and our guidance reflects that.' Ellie Mertz: 'We remain optimistic about our continued momentum.'

evidence.claim: The guidance raise is organic, not primarily attributed to FX or one-time items.
evidence.quote: The upward revision to our revenue outlook reflects meaningful progress across our growth initiatives and improvements to monetization through a simplified fee structure and our insurance programs.

review_flags.reason: The guidance raise is clear and organic, but the score of 0.50 is at the upper end of the +0.5 anchor. A reviewer may consider whether the conflict headwind and tougher comps warrant a slightly lower score, though management's confident tone and explicit raise support the current level.
